frase_gancho.texto: A city that lost its power, but not its memory.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: This last stop invites you to think about what happened afterward. Around the year eleven hundred, Chichén Itzá had already lost its role as a regional center, but the city may never have been completely abandoned. When the Spaniards arrived, people were living there or nearby. Francisco de Montejo the Younger tried to make it his capital in fifteen thirty-two and left it two years later. By fifteen eighty-eight it was a cattle ranch. Today it is a World Heritage Site and remains one of the most visited Maya cities.
